items.text: This table's last real update and its staging table's last refresh both land on the same date, 2025-10-21, confirming the load stopped there precisely, about 11 months before this analysis

The raw ShopperKit extract feeding this table is still live and updating as recently as today. The specific step that converts that raw extract into this table's own staging data, and from there into this table, is what broke on 2025-10-21, not the ShopperKit feed as a whole

All rows in this table come from ShopperKit, a retail labor and order-picking productivity system. Its column layout is an exact match to the raw ShopperKit extract table, confirming how the fields map through
No duplicate or invalid key values were found across all 1,421,899 rows

The one orchestrator found for the raw ShopperKit extract carries no scheduler header at all, unlike every comparable MoveData wrapper elsewhere in the files we have. A second, distinct ShopperKit MoveData job exists (a different XML config) with no orchestrator of its own found anywhere

items.text: Why the conversion from the raw ShopperKit extract into this table's staging data stopped on 2025-10-21, while the raw extract kept arriving normally, has not been identified
items.note: This is a precisely dateable break, not a gradual decline, which suggests a specific fixable cause (a job failure, a schema change, a decommissioned step) rather than a deliberate shutdown

items.text: Whether this table's ShopperKit labor productivity reporting is still needed by Weis has not been confirmed
items.note: If it is, this is a real, fixable gap since the underlying data is still arriving; if not, it can be excluded from the migration plan with the same confidence
